content.content:
# Headlines

How a headline is written, in any genre that links this file. A headline lets the reader judge at once whether the text is for them: it states the core of the text as briefly and precisely as it can, and it is understood on its own, with no image, standfirst or surrounding page to explain it. *Headline* here covers a text's subheadings too; for a subheading, the text is its section.

## Statement or label

A text that reports, explains, argues, decides or narrates gets a statement headline: a clause that says what the text says. A text the reader looks things up in or navigates by — a policy, a manual, opening hours, a contact page — gets a plain label naming what it holds: *Privacy policy*, where a statement would read *How we protect your data*. Everything below is about the statement headline.

## What a statement headline does

- It states the angle: the single most important message, the sentence that would remain if only one could. A subject alone is a label. Test: the headline could not head a different text on the same subject.
- It is a simple clause — subject, active verb, object where there is one — in straight word order, and in the present tense where that fits: *Council introduces free bus travel*.
- The most important keyword comes first.
- A concrete detail stands in it when the detail carries the message: a number, a date, a place. *Three schools to close this autumn* beats *Changes to school organisation*.
- The reader sees what they gain: a decision, a fact, a change. An instructional text may address the reader directly (*you*, *your*) and open on *How to*, *Why* or *Here's*.
- It is as short as the angle allows. Modifiers, repetition and filler go; a keyword that carries meaning stays. The format the text follows sets the limits.
- It sounds like something a person would say aloud.
- Its words are ones this audience knows. A technical term is the right keyword for specialists and noise for a general reader, and the same holds for names and abbreviations.
- Its tone is the text's tone, and never louder. Illness, accidents, crime and crises get a sober, understated headline; a light text can carry more personality.
- It is plain before it is clever. It works in full for a reader who misses every allusion, so a pun or a reference never carries the meaning.
- It gives the answer. Journalists hold a question headline to be the wrong form, and so does this: it is a deliberate exception, natural over a text built as questions and answers, and available where the text truly leaves the question open and the headline is meant to assert nothing.
- The verb does the work. A colon standing in for a verb, a clipped quotation and headline-speak all give way to the full clause.
- It complements what follows. Headline and standfirst, or subheading and the first sentence under it, say different things in different words.

## Every word supported

A headline claims only what its text claims. Every figure, name, claim and conclusion in it is in the text, at the text's own strength: never sharper, never more general, never a conclusion the text does not draw. A reader who finishes the text finds that the headline told the truth about it.

## Getting there

Settle the reader and the angle before wording anything. Then write three to five variants and keep the clearest, which is rarely the cleverest. Word a subheading from its whole section, once the section is written, in words its first sentence does not use.
=== REVIEW ===
# Headlines — review guidance

Read under [Headlines](headlines.md). Read the text first and say its angle to yourself in one sentence. Then read the headline against that sentence, and each subheading against its own section, and ask four questions of each. Can every word in it be supported by the text? Is the core message there? Does the tone match the seriousness of the content? Would the reader feel misled afterwards?

## Avoid

Each of these in a headline or a subheading is a finding:

- Claims, figures, names or conclusions not found in the text. A headline that sharpens, generalises or draws a conclusion the text itself does not draw is always a finding, however well it reads.
- Vague or mysterious wording that requires reading the text to understand the headline.
- A subject named with nothing said about it, where the text has an angle to state.
- Words, names and abbreviations the audience will not know.
- Partial quotes, colons in place of a verb, stilted headline-speak.
- Puns and references that fail for anyone who does not get the allusion.
- Question headlines. Where the text gives the answer, the headline gives it too. The exceptions are a text built as questions and answers, where the form is natural, and a text that truly leaves the question open, where the headline is deliberately kept from asserting anything.
- A tone more dramatic than the text's.
- The same words and phrasing in the headline and the standfirst or opening paragraph, or in a subheading and the first sentence under it. They complement each other; they do not repeat.

Name what the reader loses, and repair by rewriting the headline alone, from the text's angle and at the text's own strength. The text stays as it is.

## Leave alone

A working headline is left alone. Plain is no defect, and neither is a headline with no number or place where none carries the message, direct address in an instructional text, or an angle other than the one you would have chosen where the text supports it. A label on a reference or navigation text is correct as a label.
=== WEB ===
# Craft for five web genres

For article, case-study, column and opinion, work as a skilled Swedish journalist at the professional level of SvD, DN, DI, Fokus, Ny Teknik, Filter or Forskning & Framsteg. For web-copy, work as an experienced Swedish copywriter and UX writer trusted by leading agencies and brands. These are standards of craft, not voices to imitate.

In every target language, keep that Swedish editorial or communicative tradition in the angle, disposition, storytelling, address and tone. Think and write wholly in the target language: its Language Resource governs vocabulary, idiom, syntax, punctuation and typography. A native professional should hear a colleague, not a translation. Language choice changes the language surface, not the chosen craft.

## Web reading

Give the reader a clear angle or task and useful ways into the text. Let facts and reasoning carry explanation; choose any narrative devices for what they contribute. Headings orient according to the genre, paragraphs hold connected thoughts, and varied rhythm supports both scanning and sustained reading.

For article, case-study, column and opinion, the [article anatomy](article-anatomy.md) fixes the parts, their order and their dimensions.
=== WEBREV ===
# Reviewing web craft

Read under [the craft brief](web-craft.md). Test the text as a reader who scans, then as one who follows its reasoning. Identify the actual cost of a dense or fragmented passage before proposing a change.

Distinguish target-language fluency from editorial tradition. A Swedish angle expressed in natural English succeeds; Swedish word order in English does not. Equally, flawless local spelling does not rescue generic promotional prose from a lost journalistic purpose. Preserve successful genre-specific voice and structure instead of standardising them.

    "composition": {
      "source": "sv",
      "content": "Swedish is a V2 language: the finite verb is the second constituent of a main clause, so fronting anything at all pushes the subject behind the verb. Write *I morgon åker vi till Malmö*, never *I morgon vi åker till Malmö*. This is the single most common structural tell of a text drafted in English and rendered into Swedish.

Compounds are written as one word. *Kvalitetssäkring*, *kundtjänstmedarbetare*, *miljökonsekvensbeskrivning*. Splitting them is not a stylistic choice in Swedish and often changes the meaning outright — *en rökfri miljö* and *en rök fri miljö* are different claims. Where a compound grows unreadably long, rewrite it into a prepositional phrase rather than splitting it.

Definiteness is marked twice. An adjective before a definite noun takes both the front article and the noun's suffix: *den nya rapporten*, *det stora huset*, *de svenska kunderna*. English has one article and drafts translated from it routinely lose one of the two Swedish markers.

The s-passive is the ordinary Swedish passive and is shorter than its periphrastic alternative: *rapporten skickas på fredag*, not *rapporten blir skickad på fredag*. Both exist; the s-form is the unmarked one, and the *bli*-form carries a change-of-state reading that is often not intended.

*Du* is the default address in Swedish prose, including business and journalism. *Ni* to a single reader is either archaic or a deliberate distancing, and reads as a translation from a language that has a formal pronoun.

*Man* is a fallback rather than the ordinary generic pronoun. It is justified where the agent genuinely is anybody at all or is genuinely unknown, and where naming one would claim more than the material carries. Where the sentence has a real subject to hand — the reader, the writer, the organisation, the profession, the study — that subject is what the sentence takes. A text that reaches for *man* with any of those available reads as evasive, and it is usually where an English draft's *you*, *we*, or passive has landed rather than anything the writer chose.

Speech that the text reports is ordinarily set with a speech dash rather than in quotation marks: an interview answer, a remark at a meeting, anything a person said that the text renders readable. A writer reaches for quotation marks where the phrasing itself is the point — where it is what is new, where it is disputed, or where the text is about how the thing was said. What each of the two marks promises a reader, and what that makes each of them a claim about, is settled in Mechanics; this scope says only which one an ordinary Swedish text reaches for first.

Genitive takes a bare *s* with no apostrophe: *Kntnts kunder*, *Sveriges riksdag*. A name already ending in *s*, *x*, or *z* takes nothing at all: *Anders bok*, *Marx teori*.

Swedish tolerates a shorter sentence than English does and punishes subordination harder. Prefer a main clause with a fronted adverbial to a long relative construction, and prefer a verb to a nominalisation: *när kommunen beslutade* over *vid kommunens beslutsfattande*.

Reach for the established Swedish term where one exists and the field actually uses it — *återkoppling*, *underlag*, *avstämning* — but do not purge the loanwords a professional reader expects. A text that writes *dator* and *webbplats* naturally is Swedish; a text that hunts down every English term and replaces it with a coinage nobody says is not."
    },
    "review": {
      "source": "sv",
      "content": "Read for särskrivning first. A split compound is the error a Swedish reader notices before anything else, and generated or dictated text produces them in bulk.

Check the word order of every clause that opens with something other than the subject. A fronted adverbial, object, or subordinate clause must be followed immediately by the finite verb.

Nominal style is the characteristic failure of Swedish institutional prose. *Genomförande av en utvärdering av verksamheten* is three nouns doing the work of one verb; *utvärdera verksamheten* says it. Look for *-ande*, *-ning*, and *-else* nouns paired with a colourless verb — *ske*, *utföra*, *genomföra*, *möjliggöra* — and give the sentence its real verb back.

Watch the heavy pre-modifier: *den av kommunen beslutade planen*, *de i rapporten redovisade siffrorna*. It is grammatical and it is bureaucratic. Unpack it into a relative clause: *planen som kommunen beslutade om*.

Prepositional filler multiplies in Swedish official prose: *i syfte att* for *för att*, *avseende* and *gällande* for *om*, *utifrån* for *enligt* or *efter*, *i samband med* for *när*. Each costs words and none adds meaning.

Check that the register is one register. Swedish shifts sharply between *ni*-formality, *du*-directness, and youth-informal, and a text that mixes them reads as assembled rather than written.

Check reported speech for text-internal inconsistency in its quotation form. Fluent wording alone does not show that a quotation was repaired; without the source, leave that provenance claim unjudged. A change of mark may distinguish exact wording from rendered speech, so diagnose it only where the text gives grounds for a conflicting reading.

Read for the loan that arrived with the draft rather than with the field. *Regulatorer* is *tillsynsmyndigheter* or *myndigheter*, *adressera* in the sense of taking something up is *ta upp* or *behandla*, *leverera* in the sense of giving is *ge* or *erbjuda*, *metrik* is *mätvärde* or *nyckeltal*, and an *approach* is an *angreppssätt* or an *ansats*. The pairs are illustrative rather than a list to work through: which loans a Swedish text keeps is settled in Composition, and what a review adds is noticing the ones that are there because the sentence was thought in English.

Look for the English participle rendered mechanically as an *-ande* form. *Ökande kostnader* is Swedish; a paragraph in which every subject carries an *-ande* modifier is an English draft in Swedish clothes.

Finally, check the sentence rhythm the way a Swedish reader hears it: known information before new, one main idea per sentence, and no clause postponed behind three others."
    },
    "anti-slop": {
      "source": "sv",
      "content": "Openings that mark generated Swedish: *I dagens snabbrörliga värld*, *I en tid då*, *I en värld där*, *Det är viktigt att notera att*, *Låt oss dyka ner i*, *Låt oss titta närmare på*. Cut them; the sentence after them is the real opening.

Closings of the same kind: *Sammanfattningsvis*, *Avslutningsvis kan vi konstatera att*, *I slutändan handlar det om*, *Framtiden får utvisa*. A Swedish text that has made its point stops.

The imported false contrast: *Det handlar inte bara om X – det handlar om Y*, *Inte bara ... utan också ...*, *Det är inte X. Det är Y.* as a paragraph of its own. The construction exists in Swedish, but its density in generated text is the tell.

Metaphor stock: *en resa*, *navigera i landskapet*, *nyckeln till framgång*, *hörnstenen i*, *ta det till nästa nivå*, *game changer*, *att verkligen förstå kraften i*. These arrive as a set rather than because the writer meant any of them.

Superlative inflation: *revolutionerande*, *banbrytande*, *otroligt kraftfull*, *helt avgörande*, *oöverträffad*. Swedish general-interest prose is understated, and a text that reaches for these in every paragraph reads as advertising copy whatever it was meant to be.

Connective adverbs at the head of every paragraph — *Dessutom*, *Vidare*, *Följaktligen*, *Därtill*, *Sammantaget* — are a generation tell when they become a template for the text's progression.

A concentration of the objective punctuation errors identified in Mechanics is also evidence of English punctuation carried into generated Swedish. Refer to that scope for the forms; this scope does not restate them.

The triad reflex: *snabbt, enkelt och säkert*, *tydligt, tryggt och tillgängligt*. Three adjectives where the writer had one thing to say.

Hedging translated wholesale: *Det är värt att notera*, *Det bör understrykas*, *Det är viktigt att komma ihåg*, *Som alltid gäller att*. Swedish has the constructions; a text that opens four paragraphs with them is not hedging, it is padding.

Empty attribution: *studier visar*, *experter menar*, *det är allmänt känt att*, with nobody named. In Swedish as in any language, an unattributed authority is a claim the writer has not made."
    }
  }

This script counts them and exposes heading/following-text pairs with lexical overlap for the editorial agent to judge. ADR-0209 records why counted dimensions belong to a script rather than to the agent reading them. ## The command line uv run --no-cache --no-project article_anatomy.py `` may be `-`, which reads the text from standard input, so a response-targeted run needs no scratch file. The form is read off the text itself: HTML where it carries block tags (`

`-`

`, `

`) and no ATX heading line, Markdown otherwise. The command line goes to `argparse` as in the Library's other engines — the machine-readable refusals here are about the text rather than about the line, so there is no JSON refusal for a malformed invocation to travel in. ## The exit status is the verdict `0` measured, and every counted requirement holds. `1` measured, and at least one fails. `2` not measured. All three print one JSON object on stdout, and a refusal carries `ok: false`, a stable `code` — `unreadable-input`, `empty-text` or `no-structure` — and a `message`. ## What is read as what Leading YAML frontmatter is skipped and never parsed. What remains is read as blocks: a heading (ATX or setext in Markdown, `h1`-`h6` in HTML), a paragraph, a code block, or `other`, which is a list, a quotation, a table, an image, raw HTML or a comment. Only headings and paragraphs enter a limit; every other block is reported under the part it sits in and counted in none. The headline is the first level-1 heading. The standfirst, the byline and the lead lie between it and the first level-2 heading, and the byline is the first paragraph there of at most twelve words that does not end in `.`, `!`, `?` or `…`. Paragraphs before it are the standfirst and those after it the lead; where no paragraph has that shape the byline is reported missing, the first paragraph is taken as the standfirst and the rest as the lead. The answer names which block was taken as which, so a Skill can overrule it — as it has to where a text opens on a byline-shaped dramatic line standing before the real byline, which is the line this rule finds. Each level-2 heading opens a section running to the next one, and the last section is the ending. Text is measured as the reader sees it: Markdown emphasis, code and link syntax stripped, HTML reduced to its text with entities decoded, whitespace collapsed and the result normalised to NFC. Characters are code points, spaces included. A word is a whitespace-separated token holding at least one letter or digit, so a lone dash is no word. Sentences are split on terminal punctuation and are always reported as `sentences_estimate`, an abbreviation ending a sentence as far as any splitter can tell. ## The shape of the answer `ok`, `format`, `conforms`, `failures`, `norms`, `typical`, `parts` and `heading_pairs`. Each entry of `failures` and of `norms` carries `part` — `headline`, `standfirst`, `byline`, `lead`, `sections` or `section ` — `rule` in the anatomy's words, `measured` as a figure in words, and `text`, which is the text measured or `null` where the part is absent. No rule string is shared by a failure and a norm, so the strength of a statement is readable off the entry. `typical` carries `paragraphs`, `paragraphs_of_two_or_three_sentences`, `sections` and `sections_of_two_or_three_paragraphs`. `parts` carries `headline`, `standfirst`, `byline`, `lead`, `sections` and `other`, and a part nothing was found for is `null`. `headline` and a section's `subheading` carry `text`, `characters` and `words`; `byline` carries `text` and `words`, the anatomy giving it no dimension; `standfirst`, `lead` and a section's paragraphs carry their opening words as `text` beside `words` and `sentences_estimate`, and `standfirst` and `lead` also carry `paragraphs`, their figures covering every paragraph they hold. `other` names each remaining block's `part` — `before the headline`, `standfirst`, `lead`, `section `, or `front` where no byline settles which side of it a block stands — and its opening `text`. `heading_pairs` is unjudged evidence, independent of `failures`, `norms`, `conforms` and the exit status. Each entry carries `id`, `kind`, the complete visible `heading` and `following` text, and `shared_words`. The first entry's id and kind are `headline-standfirst`; it joins every standfirst paragraph with two newlines. Subsequent ids are `subheading-1`, `subheading-2`, etc., in document order across levels 2–6, with kind `subheading-first-sentence-estimate`. Ids survive rewording and equivalent Markdown/HTML, but inserting or removing a subheading renumbers later ones. They identify positions within a measurement, not persistent document objects. For each subheading, the first paragraph before the next heading of any level supplies the sentence estimate; intervening non-prose blocks are skipped. The estimate ends at the first `.`, `!`, `?` or `…` followed by optional closing quotes/brackets and whitespace. Closing marks remain in the visible text. Without such a boundary, the whole first paragraph is the estimate, even an unterminated fragment. Abbreviations such as `Dr. Vik` and ellipses can split prematurely; a decimal such as `3.5` does not split. No language-specific sentence parser is implied. A missing member is `null`; a first paragraph with no letter or digit is unpairable and supplies `null`, never a later paragraph or another section's prose. The structural `parts` still show what was parsed, and callers check ambiguous or missing pairs against the full text. Overlap tokenization is separate from dimension word counts: casefold each visible text, normalize to NFC, then take maximal Unicode alphanumeric runs (`[^\\W_]+`). Punctuation, underscores and whitespace separate tokens, including apostrophes and hyphens. Shared words are the unique intersection, sorted by Unicode code point; repeated occurrences count once, with no stop-word removal, stemming, synonyms or similarity score. `shared_words` is `null` when a member is `null`, and `[]` when both are present but share no tokens. The visible text keeps its original wording, case and punctuation beside the normalized words. A repeated name or subject word can be necessary; an echo can paraphrase with no shared word. Neither observation is an automatic finding. **Under ett åtta veckor långt försök hos Elm Quay var tiden till tilldelning två arbetsdagar mot tre tidigare, enligt kundens försöksanteckning. Arbetsbelastningen var samtidigt olika, och skillnaden kan inte tillskrivas programvaran. Arbetsledaren Maya Lind skulle ändra en sak.**

Maya Lind har ett förbehåll.

Run the resolver with `UV_NO_CACHE=1 UV_NO_PROJECT=1` and a fresh private `TMPDIR`, removing that directory afterwards, including on failure. Load no mechanics guidance and correct no spelling, punctuation, or grammar: a mechanical pass runs after you, and work you do there is work done twice.

**What you change, and what you preserve.** Repair what the findings name and nothing else. Every difference between the text you return and the text above is traced to a finding, or to what repairing a finding required, before this round is accepted, and a difference that traces to no finding is restored from the text you received — so a phrase you improved outside a finding is work that will be undone. Preserve everything the findings do not concern: every sentence, every fact, every quotation, every code sample, every heading, every piece of formatting and every line of frontmatter among them comes back exactly as you received it — a repair that improves a paragraph nobody complained about is a change nobody asked for and nobody will review. A code sample — a fenced block, an indented block, or an inline code span — is quoted material rather than the text's own prose: its contents are read past rather than read against the rules, so nothing inside one is a finding and nothing inside one is changed, the docstrings, comments, and string literals among them. Prose about code is ordinary prose and is read like every other sentence. Where a finding can be repaired several ways, make the smallest change that removes it. Where a finding names something you cannot repair without inventing a fact, changing what the text claims, or altering a quotation's meaning, stance, certainty or distinctive wording, leave that passage alone and say so: this text is answerable to material you do not have, and a plausible invention is worse than an unrepaired finding.

**A defect of your own costs the whole round.** The review that follows you establishes whether this text has a defect it did not have when you received it — a headline or a heading claiming more than the text claims, a heading repeating the passage under it, a limit your repair dropped. Where it establishes one, the whole round is rejected: the text you received is restored entire, nothing you did survives however much else you repaired, and no fresh attempt follows. So a finding you cannot repair without creating another one is a finding you leave and say so, exactly as you would one you cannot repair without inventing a fact — an unrepaired finding a person can settle costs less than a repair that has to be thrown away with everything beside it.

**What a repair may take with it, and what it may not.** A finding names a defect, and what a repair removes is that defect. Where the defect a finding names is the whole of the passage — an opening that would sit in front of any text, a closing that restates what the reader has just read, a claim credited to nobody that the text cannot source — removing it may be the repair, and any claim removed with it must be named in your return. That stops at a sentence whose work is to bound what the text asserts — that something is not measured, not claimed, not witnessed or not general, or that the text is an observation of a document rather than a scene from an occasion. Remove or weaken one only where the finding names a defect inside the sentence, and only where a sentence you keep still states that limit in full, so the text bounds what it claims exactly as far as it did, or where the limit contradicts another passage of the same text. Otherwise leave it exactly as it stands and say so. Where the passage carries a claim beside the defect — a fact, an observation, the point the passage exists to make — the smallest change is the one that leaves that claim standing, and deleting the passage entire is not that change. And where you can see no way to remove the defect that does not take the claim with it, leave the passage alone and say so, exactly as you would a finding you cannot repair without inventing a fact: a person can give that claim what it needs or let it go, and a round that deletes it leaves them nothing to weigh. That judgement is about the passage in front of you and never about how much of the text is left — a short text is no licence to leave a finding standing, and a long one is no licence to go on cutting.

A repair at a punctuation joint can be the smallest change even when the finding names the implication created there rather than punctuation itself. In *We finished in March, the finance team got a new reporting tool the same month.*, the defect is the implication created by joining unrelated claims, not either claim. Repair it as *We finished in March. The finance team got a new reporting tool the same month.*: splitting at the joint removes the implication and keeps the reporting-tool fact. Do the same wherever the named defect is confined to a joint; do not delete either side or supply a relationship the text does not establish. This example does not admit a wider mechanics pass: it identifies the smallest repair for the finding already in hand.

Before you return the text, compare it before and after, claim by claim. Every claim you received must still appear with its scope, certainty, attribution, chronology, causality and meaning intact unless the finding named the whole claim as the defect; that exception does not reach a sentence whose work is to bound what the text asserts, which goes only on the two conditions above, and the number or concentration of findings changes nothing about that check. The concentrated anti-slop case makes the boundary visible: removing its patterns must not discard its claims about meeting load, documentation, decisions, satisfaction, distributed work, adoption conditions, or the synchronous/asynchronous trade-off. Repair the patterns around those claims. If one cannot be separated from its pattern, keep it and report the finding unresolved; never compress several content-bearing passages into a cleaner summary.

Where the text is an `article`, a `case-study`, a `column` or an `opinion`, measure it before you return it: run `uv run "/private/var/folders/cs/vgp_x_353zd9frkjpysp7zdw0000gn/T/kntnt-editorial-388-run-3_r4msyu/home/.claude/skills/kntnt/library/scripts/article_anatomy.py" -` with the complete corrected text on stdin, under the same `UV_NO_CACHE=1 UV_NO_PROJECT=1` and fresh private `TMPDIR` terms as the resolver above. Exit 0 says only that the counted requirements hold. Exit 1 names each counted requirement of the article anatomy that fails, with the part, the rule and the figure measured: repair the ones a finding named and the ones your own repair introduced, then measure again; a requirement the text was already failing when it reached you, and that no finding names, is left exactly as it stands like everything else the findings do not concern. Exit 2 says the script could not measure the text, and your return says so. Read every `heading_pairs` entry against the complete candidate and the loaded headline contract before returning, whatever the exit status: judge whether each part adds different information in different wording. Necessary repeated names and topic words can be legitimate, and a paraphrased echo can share no words; `shared_words` alone never authorizes a change or creates a finding. Verify absent or ambiguous sentence estimates against the text; on exit 2 inspect the pairs by hand. Repair echoes named by the findings or introduced by your own correction by wording the heading from its whole text or section without strengthening its claims, then measure again. An unrelated pre-existing echo stays as received and is reported in your return, with the pair and reader loss; the evidence does not expand your correction authority. Report any echo you cannot repair within that authority the same way.

**What you return.** The complete corrected text and a short note of which findings you repaired and which you left, with the reason for each you left. Where any repair removed a passage carrying a claim, name every removed claim and say which finding made the claim itself the defect, and name every changed claim the same way — one you left standing with its scope, certainty, attribution, chronology, causality or meaning moved, and the finding the repair that moved it answered; reporting a removal never makes an impermissible one acceptable. The complete text: not a diff, not the changed passages, not a description of what you did. Return no commentary inside the text itself.

# Elm Quays arbetsledare skulle göra försöket igen

**Enligt kundens försöksanteckning var tiden till tilldelning hos Elm Quay två arbetsdagar under försöket, mot tre tidigare. Arbetsbelastningen var samtidigt olika, och skillnaden kan inte tillskrivas programvaran. Arbetsledaren Maya Lind skulle ändra en sak.**

Elm Quay registrerade 31 ärenden.

## Arbetsledaren ser nytta i en gemensam bild av ärendena

Maya Lind har ett förbehåll.

– Att ha en gemensam bild av ärendena hjälper oss, men jag skulle lägga till en vecka för förberedelser, säger Maya Lind, arbetsledare hos kunden.

## Tilldelningen tog två arbetsdagar, men arbetsbelastningen var olika

Enligt kundens försöksanteckning registrerades 31 ärenden under åtta veckor, med akuta ärenden undantagna. Tiden till tilldelning var två arbetsdagar jämfört med tre tidigare. Anteckningen säger att arbetsbelastningen var olika och att skillnaden inte kan tillskrivas programvaran.

– Jag skulle välja att göra försöket igen, säger Lind.

Kundcaset publiceras av leverantören Svale.

---

**Repaired**

- **F1** — Headline rewritten from the text's own angle at its own strength: the customer's appraisal, which the text carries verbatim in Lind's quotation. No causal claim about the software, no supplier voice, no value judgement. 48 characters, 7 words.
- **F2, F3** — The standfirst was rewritten as a self-contained summarising paragraph (34 words) carrying the trial note's assignment figures, the note's limitation, and what the reader gains from reading on. The duplicated sentence is gone, and the standfirst no longer repeats the lead or opens on the same word ("Enligt" / "Elm"). The measurement no longer reports the "both open on 'elm'" norm departure.
- **F5, F6** — The sentence "Vi på Svale är världsledande på att skapa framgång, och kunden stod hjälplös innan vi kom." was removed entire; both findings named the whole of it as the defect and it carried no other claim. **Claims removed:** that Svale is world-leading at creating success, and that the customer was helpless before the supplier arrived.
- **F7** — Subheading reworded from the whole section and attributed to the named speaker instead of asserting a shared picture as established fact. It no longer shares wording with the sentence under it (shared_words now empty).
- **F8** — The bridge's pre-echo was removed. It now prepares the quotation ("Maya Lind har ett förbehåll.") instead of saying its content in advance; the attribution stays, and the judgement about the shared picture is carried in full by the quotation itself, which is untouched.
- **F9** — Subheading rewritten from its section: it states the measured figure together with the note's qualification, so it draws no conclusion the section takes back.
- **F10** — "Vår programvara orsakade därför hela förbättringen." was removed entire; the finding named the whole causal claim as the defect and it carried nothing else. **Claim removed:** that the supplier's software caused the whole improvement. Nothing else in the results paragraph was touched, and the limiting sentence about differing workload and non-attribution stands exactly as received.

**Left unrepaired**

- **F4 (byline)** — Still absent; the measurement still reports `part: "byline", measured: "absent"` (exit 1). Neither the text, its metadata nor the assignment names an author, so filling it would mean inventing one. Left unfilled and reported, as the finding directs.
- **F11 (call to action)** — The ending still has no call to action. No offers, links or contact routes are supplied, so one cannot be written without invention. The bounding sentence "Kundcaset publiceras av leverantören Svale." was kept exactly as received, as the finding directs.
- **F12 (customer background)** — What Elm Quay does, what problem prompted the work, and what was introduced are nowhere in the material. Filling the gap would require inventing facts; reported as a gap.

**Measurement** — `article_anatomy.py` exits 1 on the returned text with a single failure, the pre-existing missing byline (F4). No norm departures remain (the original "both open on 'elm'" is gone). All three `heading_pairs` were read against the full candidate: `subheading-1` and `subheading-2` now share no words with the sentence under them and each adds different information in different wording; `headline-standfirst` shares only "elm", "försöket" and "skulle" — a necessary name, the subject word, and a modal — while the headline states the supervisor's appraisal and the standfirst states the measured figures and their limitation.
The correction round returned. Now I verify it myself — difference tracing, claim comparison, and a full re-review with the anatomy measured rather than read.

---
name: proofread
description: Correct only mechanical language errors — spelling, grammar, punctuation, agreement, inflection, duplicated or missing words, and locale mechanics — in one supplied text, preserving its wording, meaning, tone, structure, formatting, and metadata. Start it on your own only when a specific text is at hand and the request either uses a proofreading term (proofread, spell-check, copyedit, fix the typos, korrekturläs, rätta stavfelen) or is unambiguously limited to mechanical language errors. Not for a request to edit, rewrite, polish, improve, tighten, or review a text — each of those asks for changes this Skill refuses to make. A user may also invoke it by name at any time.
disable-model-invocation: false
argument-hint: '[--language=<language>] ([--output=response|<path>] [<text>|<path>|<url>] | --in-place[=on|off] <path>) [-- <instruction>]'
compatibility: Requires uv
metadata:
  kntnt.internal: "true"
  kntnt.binaries: "uv"
  kntnt.skills: ""
  kntnt.externals: ""
  kntnt.capabilities: ""
---

# proofread

Correct the mechanical language errors in one supplied Text Artifact, and change nothing else about it.

Run `UV_NO_CACHE=1 UV_NO_PROJECT=1 uv run "$HERE/scripts/invoke.py"` — `$HERE` is the directory that holds this SKILL.md — with everything the user typed after `/proofread`, verbatim and however many lines, on stdin. Exit 0: do what it prints. On any other exit, if you introduced a known construction error and can correct it while preserving the user's request and authority, account for effects already produced, submit the corrected invocation through the same shim, and continue from the failed boundary; a refusal before the operation starts consumes no operation. Otherwise show what it printed to the user verbatim and stop. Never repair input the user supplied, or automatically retry exact help, an unmet dependency, an unrelated failure, or a failure whose origin or valid correction is unknown.

Run every UV command in this Skill with a fresh private directory as `TMPDIR`, and remove that directory after the command, including when it fails. The private directory belongs to that one command and no other run, so cleanup removes only files this run created.

A model-invoked run changes only how the Skill starts. Once started, it takes the specific Text Artifact the current turn identifies as the omitted operand and enters the same numbered steps as invocation by name. The paths join before loading any language or editorial resource; the trigger wording is not a second source of rules or an alternate execution path.

Where no Formal Invocation carries an Output Target, settle it from the current turn before correcting or writing. An unnamed destination resolves to the response, and a file mentioned only as the location of the errors names no destination: the verbs *fix* and *correct* apply to the named errors, not to the file containing them. Thus `Fix the spelling and grammar mistakes in case.md` delivers to the response. A turn that explicitly names the response or a path other than the source as the destination selects that Output Target; for example, `Write the corrected text to corrected.md` selects corrected.md as a separate Output Target. A turn that asks for the file itself to be changed selects In-place Editing only when it explicitly names that file as the object of the change or as the destination of the corrected text; for example, `Update case.md with the grammar corrections` selects In-place Editing. It remains subject to every refusal that editing mode already carries, including inline text, a URL, an uploaded or read-only source, more than one text, and a simultaneous separate Output Target. A request to save, apply, or persist the corrections without naming where they go is materially ambiguous about the destination: `Fix the grammar errors in case.md and save the corrections` asks which destination the caller intends and writes nothing. For that case and any other material ambiguity about the destination, ask which destination the caller intends and write nothing.

## Arguments

The operand is the Text Artifact: inline text, one local path, or one URL, and exactly one of them — several paths, a glob reaching more than one file, or a directory of texts is more than one. Where the invocation carries no operand, it is the single text the current turn identifies.

`--language=<language>` names the language or locale whose mechanics apply. Any spelling the Collection's resolver reaches is accepted — a canonical code (`sv`, `en_GB`), a case or separator variant of one (`en-GB`, `EN_GB`), a curated alias (`BrE`, `brittisk engelska`), or an ordinary description of a language in any language.

`--output=response|<path>` names the Output Target. `response` is the default and the value `response` states it explicitly; anything else is one filesystem path. It and In-place Editing name two destinations for one text, which is why no form carries both.

`--in-place[=<value>]` selects In-place Editing. It accepts `yes`, `on`, and `true` against `no`, `off`, and `false`; bare `--in-place` means `on`, `--in-place=off` has the same effect as omitting the option, and the default is `off`.

## Steps

1. Settle the single Text Artifact and the options from the JSON. A value outside what `## Arguments` admits — `--in-place` outside its vocabulary, or more than one Text Artifact — is refused as `$LIBRARY/references/invocation-envelope.md` says: correct nothing, write nothing, and stop. Done when one Text Artifact and a valid set of options are in hand, or you have stopped.
2. Settle the destination before anything is corrected, following `$LIBRARY/references/delivery.md`. Make every refusal that contract names by reading alone — In-place Editing together with a separate Output Target, an output path equal to the input path, In-place Editing against inline text or a URL or a source that is not a writable local file, and a destination whose parent directory does not exist — so that a refusal has nothing written behind it. Done when the destination is settled, or you have stopped.
3. Read the Text Artifact's leading YAML frontmatter where it has any, and look in it for one top-level `kntnt` map. That map is the only Kntnt configuration a document carries; `language`, `lang`, `genre`, `technique`, and every other key outside it are the document's own fields, whatever they are named and whatever they hold. Read `language` out of the map and nothing else out of it. The map is never required: a Text Artifact carrying none is proofread exactly like one that carries a complete one, its absence refusing nothing and leaving the language to the levels below it in step 4. Done when the artifact's recognized language value is known to be present, absent, or unreachable.
4. Resolve the language, taking the first of these that answers: the `--language` value; the recognized `kntnt` map's `language` value from step 3; the current Contextual Instruction; applicable Conversation Context; then the language of the Text Artifact itself, which is what inference reads and what the default already is. Suppression is that precedence working rather than an error: a Contextual Instruction every higher level has already settled leaves nothing for it to settle, and the run continues rather than refusing it as unaddressable guidance. Where saying so is useful, the delivery names the suppressed instruction beside the resolved configuration. Where that language is materially ambiguous or mixed — no dominant language, or alternation inside paragraphs — ask which language to proofread in rather than choosing one. Nothing has been written yet, so asking costs nothing to undo. Done when exactly one selector is in hand, or you have asked.
5. If step 3 found a recognized `kntnt` map whose `language` value no installed resource answers to, and `--language` supplied no value, report it as unusable artifact metadata: name the value, say that it is neither a canonical code nor an installed alias, and stop. Do not read it as the code it resembles. A `--language` value settles the parameter and suppresses this, the unusable map then being none of the run's business. Done when the run has stopped, or the metadata is not in the way.
6. Run `uv run --no-cache --no-project "$LIBRARY/scripts/languages.py" resolve --scope=mechanics "<selector>"`. Exit 0: take the reported `code` as the resolved language and the `mechanics` scope as this run's language-specific rules. A non-zero exit means the selector reached no single installed resource — interpret the human description semantically, propose one candidate from `uv run --no-cache --no-project "$LIBRARY/scripts/languages.py" list`, and verify it through the same `resolve` command; ask only where no unique installed candidate can be established. Then load `$LIBRARY/references/editorial/mechanics.md`, the shared mechanics contract, which holds the rules of objective correctness that do not depend on the language; it and the resolved scope together are this run's rules, and the scope is the more specific of the two wherever they meet. That one document is the whole of what is admitted from the Collection's editorial resources: load no base contract, no genre, no technique, and no anti-slop catalogue, load no other scope, and read no composition, review, or anti-slop guidance from anywhere. Done when the contract and the mechanics scope are both in hand, or you have stopped.
7. Correct every objective mechanical error in the resolved language, reading the text yourself: misspellings, grammatical errors, punctuation errors, agreement between subject and verb or noun and modifier, wrong inflection, a duplicated word, a word plainly missing, and the locale's own conventions for dates, numbers, currency, and quotation as the mechanics scope states them, together with everything the shared mechanics contract holds. Correct all of them — a mechanical pass that leaves mechanical errors behind is a pass the user has to make again. Before this step is done, make an agreement-only re-read of every ordinary-prose sentence after the other corrections. Check agreement in both directions between subject and verb and between noun and modifier; in Swedish, `olika bild` must become `olika bilder`. Make that same re-read whether `--language` named the language or another level of the precedence settled it. A resolved locale establishes its date conventions but not what ambiguous source fields meant: `3/4` stays exactly `3/4` under both `en_GB` and `en_US` unless the Text Artifact itself establishes one reading; never expand or reorder it solely from locale. A grammatically valid word-as-word phrase such as `the word probably` remains unmarked: add no quotation marks or other emphasis unless the loaded rules identify an objective error. A code sample — a fenced block, an indented block, or an inline code span — is quoted material rather than the text's own prose: its contents are read past rather than read against the rules, so nothing inside one is a finding and nothing inside one is changed, the docstrings, comments, and string literals among them. Prose about code is ordinary prose and is read like every other sentence. Introduce no spellchecker, grammar service, or scanner of your own; the resolver above is the only script this Skill runs. Done when the mechanical errors you can identify are corrected.
8. Change nothing else. Wording, meaning, tone, register, argument, structure, factual content, formatting and markup, code and its contents, links, and metadata all come through untouched, and the frontmatter comes through byte for byte — a language value you were entitled to read is read and left exactly where it is, no `kntnt` map is added or removed, and nothing is reordered. A preference is not an error, and the rules step 6 put in hand are what says which is which: what neither of them names as an error comes through untouched, however tempting it is, and what either of them does name is corrected however deliberate it looks. A sentence improved here is the failure this Skill exists to prevent: mechanical correction was requested, and mechanical correction is the whole of what is delivered. Done when the diff you are about to deliver is mechanical throughout.

Nothing here is a preference. A rule belongs in this document only where the text is wrong whatever the writer intended, and only where it would be wrong in the same way in any language. Spelling, inflection, agreement, the language's own punctuation, and its conventions for dates, numbers, currency, and quotation all turn on the language and belong to that language's resource. Where a language defaults more strictly or more loosely than a rule below, its own guidance says so, and what it says about itself wins.

The examples are English because this document is, and they are patterns rather than strings. Apply each by what it does in the target language rather than by the words it happens to use.

## Clause boundaries

Two independent clauses joined by a comma alone are an error where the second does not explain, specify, restate, or stand in direct contrast to the first. *The project will be expensive, it starts in the spring* puts two statements in one sentence that have nothing to do with each other beyond sitting there together: the reader takes the comma as a signal that the sentence continues, and meets a new subject and a new verb instead. Two clauses run together with no punctuation at the joint at all are the same error, and take the same correction.

The same joint is not an error where the second clause does explain, specify, restate, or contrast with the first. *The bug was not in the parser, it was in a silent retry* is the negative-positive contrast, where the comma is what holds the two halves together as one statement, and separating them would break a single thought into two. *We shipped it anyway, nobody had a better idea* specifies the first clause with the reason behind it. Both are established usage rather than tolerated looseness, and a pass that corrects them has changed how the sentence reads without being asked to.

Judge a joint by whether the clauses cohere, and not by their length, by how formal the text is, or by how the text punctuates elsewhere. Where the reading is genuinely open — where a careful reader could defend the joint — the comma stands, because what this rule reaches is the boundary that misleads and not the boundary that is merely informal.

Correct an erroneous joint at the joint and nowhere else: the comma becomes a period or a semicolon, and nothing else about the sentence moves. Do not reorder the clauses, do not merge them into one, and do not supply a conjunction — *and*, *but*, and *so* each assert a relation between the two clauses, and the writer asserted none. Neither half is rewritten, split, or tightened on the way past. Where more than one of a period and a semicolon would serve, the period is the safer of the two, since it claims nothing about how closely the statements are related.

## Quotation

Quoted matter reaches a reader in one of three settings, and the setting decides what the punctuation and capitalisation around it have to do. A quotation is run into a sentence, set off as a block of its own, or reported as speech, and a reader takes each of the three as a different promise about where the sentence ends, where the source's words begin, and who is speaking. The marks are the language's. Which glyphs enclose a quotation, which side of a closing mark a stop falls on, and how speech is conventionally set are stated in the resolved language's mechanics scope and not here, and the marks in the examples below stand in for whichever ones it names. What follows holds whatever they turn out to be — which setting a quotation is in, and what that setting then requires.

A run-in quotation is part of the sentence carrying it, and the joint between the two is punctuated by what the quoted words do there. Where the quotation is introduced as an utterance of its own, a stop stands at the joint and the quotation opens the way a sentence opens: *She replied, "I'll be there."* Where the quoted words are instead a grammatical part of the host sentence — its object, its complement, a fragment the sentence reads straight through — no stop stands at the joint and the quotation takes the case the surrounding syntax needs: *She called the proposal "completely unacceptable"*, not *She called the proposal, "Completely unacceptable"*. The sentence around a run-in quotation still ends, and it ends once. A quoted sentence's own final stop and the host sentence's stop are one stop and not two, and where the quoted matter ends in a question or exclamation mark that mark stands alone and takes no comma beside it: *"Will you?" she asked*, not *"Will you?", she asked*. She said.* Which side of the closing mark the surviving stop falls on is settled by the language and not here.

A block quotation is marked by being set off, and that setting is the whole of the mark. Marks enclosing a block state the quotation a second time, and they cost the reader the one thing the block was doing for them: inside a block, marks are the source's own and are preserved as the source wrote them. Because the block itself takes no level, a quotation inside one stands at the outermost level the language has rather than at the level it would take nested inside another.

The sentence introducing a block has finished by the time the block begins, and the block ends on the quoted matter's own punctuation, so the surrounding sentence's stop does not follow the block and no part of the host sentence is left hanging past it. A source named with a block sits outside the quotation and after it; set inside, the attribution reads as something the source wrote about itself.

Reported speech is punctuated as a run-in quotation is, and what the setting adds is the layout that says who is speaking. A turn belongs to one speaker and takes a paragraph of its own, and a second speaker beginning inside the first speaker's paragraph is read as the first speaker still talking, however plainly the words belong to somebody else. Where one speaker's turn runs across more than one paragraph, the continuation is marked as the same turn, because a reader shown nothing takes the second paragraph for somebody else's turn: a new paragraph is what a change of speaker looks like in this setting. How a language marks the continuation is its own — a turn left unclosed until its last paragraph, a speech mark opening every one of them — but that the reader can tell one continued turn from two is not the language's to settle.

A quotation promises that the words inside it are the source's, and three departures from that promise are each marked where they occur. Words added or altered so that the quotation fits its host sentence — a pronoun resolved, a tense harmonised, an initial capital raised or lowered to suit the surrounding syntax — are marked as the writer's rather than the source's: *"[T]he proposal was unacceptable"*. Words left out are marked at the gap, so that the reader is not shown a continuous sentence the source never wrote: *"the proposal … was unacceptable"*. An error the source made is kept and marked as the source's — *[sic]* — because quoted matter is not the text's own, and an error corrected inside a quotation makes the quotation false about its source. That preserves nothing the rules in hand name as an error. A construction this contract or the resolved language's own mechanics guidance identifies as wrong is corrected however consistently the text commits to it, because consistency is what an established variant is judged by and never what makes something established. A text that is wrong the same way throughout is wrong throughout.

Granskningen är klar. Den mekaniska slutpassagen hittade inga fel att rätta, och inget skrevs till filsystemet — `source.md` är oförändrad.

**Upplösning:** genre `case-study` och språk `sv` från anropet. Ingen teknik tillämpades: genren anger att den inte skrivs med någon. Korrigeringsbudget 1, förbrukad på en runda, som accepterades efter omgranskning.

```markdown
# Elm Quays arbetsledare skulle göra försöket igen

**Enligt kundens försöksanteckning var tiden till tilldelning hos Elm Quay två arbetsdagar under försöket, mot tre tidigare. Arbetsbelastningen var samtidigt olika, och skillnaden kan inte tillskrivas programvaran. Arbetsledaren Maya Lind skulle ändra en sak.**

Elm Quay registrerade 31 ärenden.

## Arbetsledaren ser nytta i en gemensam bild av ärendena

Maya Lind har ett förbehåll.

– Att ha en gemensam bild av ärendena hjälper oss, men jag skulle lägga till en vecka för förberedelser, säger Maya Lind, arbetsledare hos kunden.

## Tilldelningen tog två arbetsdagar, men arbetsbelastningen var olika

Enligt kundens försöksanteckning registrerades 31 ärenden under åtta veckor, med akuta ärenden undantagna. Tiden till tilldelning var två arbetsdagar jämfört med tre tidigare. Anteckningen säger att arbetsbelastningen var olika och att skillnaden inte kan tillskrivas programvaran.

– Jag skulle välja att göra försöket igen, säger Lind.

Kundcaset publiceras av leverantören Svale.
```

## Kvarstående iakttagelser (olösta)

Budgeten tog slut medan dessa återstod. Ingen av dem kan repareras utan material som texten inte innehåller.

1. **Bylinen saknas.** Mätningen med `article_anatomy.py` ger exit 1 med `part: "byline", measured: "absent"`. Anatomin kräver delen. Varken texten, dess metadata eller anropet namnger någon författare, så den lämnas ofylld i stället för att fyllas med en uppfunnen uppgift. Läsaren vet inte vem som står för redogörelsen.
2. **Avslutningen saknar uppmaning.** Den sista delen visar inte att inledningens förväntan infriats och kallar inte läsaren till någon handling. Genren tillåter bara uppmaningar som bygger på tillhandahållna erbjudanden, länkar eller kontaktvägar, och materialet innehåller inga. Läsaren får ingen väg vidare.
3. **Kundbakgrunden saknas helt.** Texten säger inte vad Elm Quay gör, vilket problem som skulle lösas eller vad som infördes — allt sådant som genren begär för att läsaren ska förstå situationen. Luckan kan inte fyllas utan uppfunna fakta.
4. **Inledningen sätter ingen förväntan.** Den består nu av en enda siffermening och säger inte vad redogörelsen ska visa. Bristen fanns redan i den inkomna texten, där förväntan vilade helt på de två ogrundade påståendena nedan, och den kan inte repareras utan det bakgrundsmaterial som iakttagelse 3 saknar.

## Påståenderedovisning

Borttagna påståenden, med den iakttagelse vars defekt var hela påståendet:

- Att leverantörens lösning räddade Elm Quay (rubriken) — iakttagelsen om att varje ord i en rubrik ska ha stöd; texten själv avvisar orsakssambandet.
- Att Svale är världsledande på att skapa framgång — iakttagelsen om ogrundat beröm och leverantörens röst i brödtexten.
- Att kunden stod hjälplös innan leverantören kom — iakttagelsen om räddningsberättelsen som fråntar kunden agens.
- Att resultatet bevisar allt (underrubriken) — iakttagelsen om en slutsats som avsnittet självt tar tillbaka.
- Att programvaran orsakade hela förbättringen — iakttagelsen om orsak dragen ur en jämförelse före och efter, i direkt motsägelse till meningen före.
- Den ena av ingressens två identiska meningar och bryggan före citatet togs bort som ordagrann respektive innehållslig dubblering. Båda påståendena står kvar i full form på annat håll i texten: siffran i inledningen, omdömet om den gemensamma bilden i citatet.

Ändrade påståenden:

- Underrubriken **”Kunden fick en gemensam bild”** påstod som konstaterat faktum det som texten bara bär som en namngiven talares omdöme. Reparationen av ekot mellan underrubrik och avsnitt flyttade den till **”Arbetsledaren ser nytta i en gemensam bild av ärendena”** — svagare och attribuerad. Inget påstående stärktes.

## Vad körningen i övrigt ändrade

Rubrik och båda underrubrikerna skrevs om ur textens egen vinkel och med textens egen styrka, och ingressen ersattes av en självbärande sammanfattning som inte längre upprepar inledningen eller inleds med samma ord som den. Bryggan före citatet gör nu bara det en brygga ska: förbereder det. Säljande och överdrivna formuleringar togs bort tillsammans med leverantörens vi-röst i berättelsen. Citaten, sifferuppgifterna och de avgränsande meningarna — attributionen till försöksanteckningen, undantaget för akuta ärenden, uppgiften om olika arbetsbelastning med att skillnaden inte kan tillskrivas programvaran, och att kundcaset publiceras av leverantören — står ordagrant kvar. Den avslutande korrekturläsningen fann inga mekaniska fel att rätta.
